293.name: Barton Gin
293.note: Bottom shelf and tastes it. Mixer of last resort.

402.name: Bombay Sapphire Gin
402.note: Vapor-infused and gentle. Famous, but Bombay Dry has more character for less.

406.name: Boodles Gin
406.note: No citrus botanicals at all — pure juniper, nutmeg, sage. A martini gin.

447.name: Broker's Gin
447.note: The value pick of the whole list. 94 proof, proper juniper, eighteen dollars.

453.name: Buffalo Trace Bourbon
453.note: The reference point for what bourbon should cost and taste like. Grab it when you see it.

686.name: Citadelle Gin
686.note: French, nineteen botanicals, floral but the juniper still shows up. Versatile.

2265.name: Old Grand Dad 80
2265.note: The 80-proof version. Fine, but the 100 is two dollars more and much better.

2266.name: Old Grand Dad 100
2266.note: Bonded, high-rye, twenty-five dollars. The thinking person’s cheap bourbon.

2267.name: Old Grand Dad 114
2267.note: High-rye and 114 proof for thirty dollars. Spicy, hot, excellent in an old fashioned.

2281.name: Old Overholt
2281.note: The 80-proof version. Get the bonded instead.

3073.name: Virginia Gentleman
3073.note: The Virginia standby. Sentimental value exceeds flavor value.

3451.name: Tanqueray Gin
3451.note: Four botanicals, 94.6 proof, nothing wasted. The one to beat under thirty dollars.

4154.name: Seagram's Distiller's Reserve Gin
4154.note: A real step up from standard Seagram's for two dollars more.

4532.name: Wild Turkey American Honey
4532.note: Honey liqueur at 71 proof. Sweet, and not really whiskey any more.

4737.name: Bluecoat Gin
4737.note: Philadelphia, 94 proof, big organic citrus. Assertive.

5167.name: New Amsterdam Straight Gin
5167.note: Almost no juniper — closer to citrus vodka. Popular, not good.

5738.name: Four Roses Bourbon
5738.note: The yellow label. Light, floral, forgiving — good for someone new to bourbon.

5963.name: Wild Turkey 101 Rye
5963.note: 101 proof and full of baking spice. A manhattan built for it.

6169.name: Jim Beam Bourbon
6169.note: The white label. It is everywhere for a reason, and that reason is not flavor.

7355.name: Wild Turkey 81
7355.note: The softer Wild Turkey. Perfectly good; the 101 is better for five dollars more.

7507.name: High West Double Rye
7507.note: A blend of young and old rye. Peppery, complex for thirty dollars.

8317.name: Templeton Rye
8317.note: Good whiskey wrapped in a fictional Prohibition story. Priced for the story.

8337.name: Larceny Bourbon
8337.note: Wheated and easy-drinking. A gentler cousin to Weller.

8509.name: Aviation Gin
8509.note: Soft, lavender-and-sarsaparilla, juniper way in the back. Good in sours.

9157.name: Bulldog Gin
9157.note: Smooth and a bit anonymous. Poppy and dragon eye don't announce themselves.

9263.name: The Botanist Islay Dry Gin
9263.note: Twenty-two Islay botanicals, layered and herbal. The most interesting bottle under thirty.

9491.name: Fighting Cock 103
9491.note: 103 proof and unsubtle. Cheap heat, some charm.

10350.name: Seagram's Extra Dry Gin (plastic)
10350.note: Same gin, plastic bottle. Buy it for the cooler, not the bar cart.

10364.name: Jim Beam (plastic)
10364.note: White label in plastic. Mixing only.

10464.name: Seagram's Lime Twisted Gin
10464.note: Candied lime. Does the work of a gin and a mixer, badly.

10465.name: Tanqueray Rangpur Gin
10465.note: Rangpur lime built in. Genuinely good in a gin and tonic.

10579.name: Seagram's Extra Dry Gin
10579.note: Rested in oak, faintly sweet. Fine in a tall drink, dull in a martini.

10581.name: Bombay Dry Gin
10581.note: The original, not Sapphire. More juniper, less perfume, seven dollars cheaper.

10605.name: Jim Beam Black
10605.note: Older, rounder Beam. The white label with the corners sanded off.

11096.name: Kopper Kettle Golden Gin
11096.note: Virginia, oak-rested. Try it where you'd use a light whiskey.

11510.name: Jim Beam Double Oak
11510.note: Twice-barreled Beam. More oak, still Beam.

11571.name: Jim Beam Devil's Cut
11571.note: Extra barrel character. A bit hot and hollow.

11719.name: Benchmark No. 8
11719.note: Thin, but it is thirteen dollars and it is not offensive.

11896.name: Evan Williams Black
11896.note: The value benchmark under fifteen dollars. Genuinely good for what it costs.

11900.name: Evan Williams Honey
11900.note: Sweet and simple. Fine as a shot, wrong for a cocktail.

11901.name: Evan Williams Peach
11901.note: Peach candy. Mixes with lemonade, if you must.

11903.name: Evan Williams White Label
11903.note: Bottled-in-bond at 100 proof for twenty-one dollars. One of the best deals in the store.

11922.name: George Dickel Rye
11922.note: 95% rye from Indiana, charcoal-filtered in Tennessee. Consistently good.

11951.name: Henry McKenna Bourbon
11951.note: The cheap McKenna, not the 10-year bonded. Thin but honest at thirteen dollars.

11993.name: Jim Beam Rye
11993.note: The yellow-label rye. A fine well pour.

12528.name: Jim Beam Vanilla
12528.note: Vanilla syrup with a whiskey accent.

12713.name: Ancient Age (plastic)
12713.note: Bottom of the Buffalo Trace family tree. Mixer only.

13183.name: Old Overholt Bonded
13183.note: The 100-proof bonded Overholt, not the 80. Far better and only three dollars more.

13432.name: Wild Turkey 101 Bourbon
13432.note: 101 proof, big vanilla and char. Punches far above twenty-eight dollars.

13597.name: Jack Daniel's Tennessee Rye
13597.note: Softer and sweeter than most rye. Fine, unexciting.

13601.name: Old Forester 86
13601.note: The everyday Old Forester. Solid, banana-and-oak, nothing to prove.

13604.name: Old Forester Signature 100
13604.note: Bottled at 100 proof and priced like it is not. Best straight-shelf value here.

14060.name: Evan Williams Black (plastic)
14060.note: Same whiskey, plastic bottle. For the cooler, not the cabinet.

14159.name: Beefeater London Dry Gin
14159.note: The benchmark. If a recipe says 'gin', it means this. Hard to beat at $22.

14203.name: Wild Turkey 101 (plastic)
14203.note: Same whiskey as the glass bottle. Buy this one and pocket the difference.

14443.name: Schlichte Steinhager Gin
14443.note: German steinhäger — malty, closer to genever than London dry. An oddity worth trying once.

15092.name: Battle Standard 142 Navy Strength
15092.note: 114 proof Virginia. Punchy, holds its own in a cocktail.

15117.name: Caorunn Small Batch Scottish Gin
15117.note: Rowan berry and apple, crisp and dry. Excellent with a slice of red apple.

15136.name: Catoctin Creek Watershed Gin
15136.note: Loudoun County rye base, spicy and distinctive. Best Virginia gin here.

15286.name: Ragged Branch Signature
15286.note: Charlottesville, estate-grown grain. The best of the small Virginia bourbons here.

15293.name: Redemption Rye
15293.note: Straightforward MGP rye. Reliable in cocktails.

15332.name: Tinkerman's Gin
15332.note: Bright and busy, as the name promises.

15499.name: Yellowstone Select
15499.note: Well-made and a bit overlooked at this price.

15522.name: 1792 Small Batch
15522.note: Rye-forward and peppery. Holds its own in a cocktail.

15533.name: Bowman Brothers Virginia
15533.note: Made in Fredericksburg from Buffalo Trace distillate. The Virginia one worth buying.

15566.name: Commonwealth Gin
15566.note: Virginia-made, coriander-forward. Good value at seventeen dollars.

15636.name: Old Forester Rye 100
15636.note: 100 proof, bright and grassy. Excellent value.

15902.name: Virgin Bourbon 101
15902.note: Obscure, 101 proof, eighteen dollars. Worth trying once.

16338.name: Jim Beam with Highball Glass
16338.note: White label plus a glass. Buy it for the glass.

16379.name: Old Tub
16379.note: Unfiltered bonded Beam. Rougher and more interesting than the white label.

16393.name: Battle Standard 142 Barrel Finished
16393.note: Oak-finished. Interesting neat, muddy in a G&T.

16394.name: Battle Standard 142 Gin
16394.note: Virginia craft, competent across the range.

16456.name: Fords Gin
16456.note: Built by a bartender for cocktails and it shows. Best all-purpose bottle here after Tanqueray.

16462.name: Malfy Con Arancia
16462.note: Sicilian blood orange, quite sweet. Works in a spritz.

16511.name: Ungava Gin
16511.note: Bright yellow, Arctic botanicals. Novel; the novelty wears off.

17144.name: Tanqueray Sevilla Orange
17144.note: Orange Tanqueray. Better than most flavored gins, still a sidestep.

17235.name: Evan Williams 1783 Small Batch
17235.note: A real step up from Evan Williams Black for nine more dollars.

17295.name: Creek Water Whiskey
17295.note: 100 proof and rough. More attitude than whiskey.

17339.name: Leadslingers Napalm Cinnamon
17339.note: Cinnamon, aggressively. Not a sipping decision.

17408.name: Elijah Craig Straight Rye
17408.note: Softer, wheat-adjacent style of rye. Very drinkable.

17431.name: Redneck Riviera Whiskey
17431.note: Sweet and soft. Sold on the label, not the liquid.

17438.name: Southern Comfort 80
17438.note: Not bourbon and never was. Sweet fruit liqueur.

17690.name: Buffalo Trace Bourbon Cream
17690.note: A cream liqueur, not a bourbon. Good over ice or in coffee.

17724.name: Rebel 100
17724.note: Wheated at 100 proof for twenty-two dollars. Serviceable.

17792.name: Very Old Barton 100 Proof
17792.note: Seventeen dollars for bonded bourbon. Rough edges, real value.

17855.name: Ezra Brooks 99 Proof
17855.note: Bold for the money. A decent well bourbon.

17978.name: Bombay Sapphire Bramble Gin
17978.note: Blackberry Sapphire. Sweet and a bit thin.

19052.name: Brown Sugar Bourbon 103
19052.note: Cinnamon and brown sugar at 103 proof. Loud and sweet.

19094.name: Bo & Ivy Distillers Gin
19094.note: Perfectly decent, nothing to argue about.

19514.name: Rittenhouse Rye Private Barrel
19514.note: Rittenhouse from a single barrel. Same excellence, slightly more varied.

19677.name: Citadelle Jardin d'Été
19677.note: Stone fruit version. Nice, but the standard Citadelle is the better bottle.

19906.name: Cutwater Black Skimmer Rye
19906.note: Competent, a little thin for thirty dollars.

20166.name: Malfy Gin Con Limone
20166.note: Lemon-forward and easy. Basically a head start on a tom collins.

20312.name: Penelope Bourbon Four Grain
20312.note: Four-grain blend, honeyed and approachable. Popular for a reason.

20389.name: Rittenhouse Rye
20389.note: Bonded 100-proof rye for twenty-four dollars. The best cocktail whiskey in the store, full stop.

20432.name: Benchmark Single Barrel
20432.note: Pleasant and inoffensive. Varies barrel to barrel.

20447.name: Benchmark Bonded
20447.note: Bonded Buffalo Trace-adjacent bourbon for twenty-two dollars. Better than Benchmark No. 8.

20448.name: Benchmark Full Proof
20448.note: 125 proof from the Buffalo Trace mashbill for twenty-five dollars. Loud and cheap.

20553.name: Green River Kentucky Bourbon
20553.note: Newer Kentucky distillery finding its feet. Decent.

20584.name: Kopper Kettle Bonded Rye
20584.note: Virginia bonded rye. Solid local pour.

20589.name: Stellum Rye
20589.note: 116 proof, uncut. A lot of whiskey for thirty dollars.

20590.name: Stellum Bourbon
20590.note: Uncut at 116 proof for thirty dollars. Blended from good stock; add water.

21100.name: Green River Wheated
21100.note: Soft wheated pour. Pleasant, not memorable.

21914.name: Larceny Private Barrel
21914.note: Single-barrel Larceny at 92 proof. Better than the standard bottle when you find it.

21949.name: W L Weller Special Reserve
21949.note: Wheated and soft. Genuinely hard to find at shelf price — take it if the count says any.

21991.name: Highlands Dragon Navy Strength
21991.note: 114 proof. Stands up to strong mixers and doesn't vanish in a negroni.

22032.name: Very Old Barton 80
22032.note: Cheap and passable. The 100 proof is the one to get.

22846.name: Greenalls London Dry Gin
22846.note: Honest, unfussy London dry. Nothing to complain about.

23077.name: Jim Beam US Soccer Label
23077.note: White label with a different sticker. Same whiskey.

23445.name: Aviation Gin (gift set)
23445.note: Same gin as standard Aviation, with a scarf. Pay for the gin, not the scarf.

23833.name: Aviation Cranberry & Blood Orange
23833.note: A flavored spinoff. Skip it and buy the standard bottle.

23902.name: Catoctin Creek Shenandoah Pink Gin
23902.note: Rose-tinted and floral. Pleasant, less serious than the Watershed.

23977.name: Evan Williams Blackberry
23977.note: Sweet blackberry. Not a whiskey decision.

24145.name: Benchmark Rye
24145.note: 100 proof for seventeen dollars. Rough but honest.

24323.name: Engine Gin
24323.note: Italian, organic, sold in a motor-oil can. Light and citrusy; the can is half the appeal.

24793.name: Waterloo No. 9 Gin
24793.note: Austin, Texas. Lavender and pecan, gentle.

24981.name: Four Roses Bourbon 100 Proof
24981.note: The yellow label with the volume turned up. Floral, high-rye, very good.

25023.name: Boondocks 6 Year
25023.note: Six-year age statement at thirty dollars. Fair.

_readme: Jeff's ratings. Keyed on labelId (a product family, e.g. all five sizes of Tanqueray). score 0-10. style: london-dry | contemporary | navy-strength | barrel-aged | flavored | genever. source 'draft' = Claude's first pass from general consensus; change to 'jeff' once you've confirmed or overridden it. This file is the only thing here that can't be regenerated.
